At aff6cc7b a real Linux x86_64 UTM court matched the host SHA-256 for agenterm-cu and libagenterm.so, then proved ordinary-file opened-object identity, final-link no-follow/link-like identity, and typed file_inspect_failed for a missing path before releasing the VM. At 867a6a64 a real Windows x86_64 UTM court matched the host SHA-256 for agenterm-cu.exe and agenterm.dll, then proved ordinary-file opened-object identity, exact size and Windows attributes plus the same typed missing-path failure before release. These focused proofs are native ACU execution, not yet the full Linux/Windows qjswasm journeys. Package tests, strict Clippy and x86_64 Windows cargo-xwin check are green.

capabilities.acu_shape: agenterm-cu network-interfaces --max N (alias: network interfaces)
capabilities.next: execute the same public stable-prefix/schema journey on native Linux and Windows, then promote to native
capabilities.note: The shared platform facade uses getifaddrs plus ifindex on Unix and GetAdaptersAddresses plus adapter LUID on Windows. It returns stable-sorted address rows under a 10000-record scan ceiling and 1 MiB response ceiling; max is validated as 1..5000 before enumeration. Missing MAC/netmask/CIDR fields remain explicit unavailable fields. The MCU compatibility entry routes only interfaces; routes/DNS/sockets stay honest gaps.

capabilities.mcu_shape: network routes --max N with destination, gateway, interface, flags, table and metric
capabilities.acu_shape: agenterm-cu network-routes --max N (alias: network routes)
capabilities.next: run the same public qjswasm journey in Linux and Windows native courts, then promote to native
capabilities.note: The shared platform facade uses NETLINK_ROUTE on Linux, PF_ROUTE NET_RT_DUMP2 on macOS and GetIpForwardTable2 on Windows. It preserves ifindex/LUID identity, rejects interrupted or malformed snapshots, stable-sorts a 10000-record scan under a 1 MiB response ceiling, and never invokes a shell. The compatibility adapter routes the lossless --max shape. macOS public evidence cu.network-routes is green; Linux/Windows runtime evidence is not claimed yet.

capabilities.mcu_shape: network dns --max N
capabilities.next: typed active resolver/search-domain inventory; Linux must not assume resolv.conf is the complete systemd-resolved state

capabilities.mcu_shape: network dns-services --max N
capabilities.next: define per-service DNS identity separately for each OS instead of treating the current macOS networksetup shape as portable

capabilities.mcu_shape: network sockets --pid/--name/--protocol/--state/--offset/--max/--scan-max
capabilities.acu_shape: process-sockets --pid N with family/protocol/state/endpoint filters and independent scan/page bounds
capabilities.note: The identity-safe per-process slice is live. Global/name-selected system socket inventory is not inferred from it and remains a gap.
capabilities.next: add a bounded global inventory with exact process identity joins, then native courts

capabilities.mcu_shape: network probe HOST --port N --attempts N --timeout-ms N with DNS and TCP latency evidence
capabilities.acu_shape: agenterm-cu network-probe HOST --port N --attempts N --timeout-ms N (alias: network probe)
capabilities.next: restore the existing 2 MiB Windows release-size court without raising it; retain the Windows arm64 UTM/QGA pre-execution transport gap separately, then promote to native
capabilities.note: Implemented behind an invocation-owned internal helper because Windows and glibc native resolver cancellation cannot prove completed cancellation. Resolution is once/deduplicated/frozen; TCP refusal and timeout are successful unreachable observations. The same public loopback journey is green on macOS arm64, Linux arm64 plus x86_64, and Windows x86_64; all six cells compile. Windows arm64 did not start because its UTM/QGA transfer lost progress. The active qjswasm/tinyvm host surface still has no generic DNS/TCP APIs.

capabilities.acu_shape: session start|list|status|renew|end with bounded TTL, retained terminal status, closed job admission, bound-job termination and automatic owned-lock release
capabilities.note: The opaque lease is returned once; durable state and audit contain only its SHA-256 digest. Job admission rechecks the lease while holding one stable per-session cross-process gate. Explicit end commits terminal state first, stops bound jobs and releases locks; the same lease can retry incomplete cleanup without repeating completed effects.

evidence: agenterm-cu macos isolated public runtime loop
capabilities.note: Same-owner reacquisition preserves lock identity and renews expiry; another session fails typed. Session end/expiry releases the lock.

capabilities.acu_shape: current, SSH and VNC mutations accept one all-or-none request-id/session/session-lease envelope; remote identity travels only in a bounded versioned stdin envelope and is admitted by the effect-owning worker
capabilities.next: derive exact target locks for migrated consumer cohorts, then prove one non-destructive mutation and exact replay through public SSH and VNC courts on all applicable hosts

capabilities.note: Default-next orders required Accessibility before optional Screen Capture and refuses unknown status instead of guessing. Opening System Settings proves dispatcher acceptance only; it does not grant, bypass or verify user consent.
capabilities.next: prove a denied macOS permission opens the exact pane under an explicit native court, then run typed Linux and Windows public journeys

capabilities.mcu_shape: open PATH_OR_URL [--app APPLICATION] [--bg]
capabilities.acu_shape: host-open PATH_OR_URL [--app APPLICATION] [--background] (also: open)
capabilities.note: The shell-free host adapter accepts exactly one path or URL. Success means only that the native dispatcher accepted the request; replies remain verified=false because handler rendering or consumption was not observed. Target and application are represented in durable receipts by byte length and SHA-256 rather than plaintext.
capabilities.next: run handler-owned no-window fixtures in Linux and Windows native courts; unsupported application/background shapes must remain typed rather than ignored

capabilities.note: Notification title/body/subtitle are passed as bounded argv data, never shell or AppleScript source. Durable receipts store only byte lengths and SHA-256. Dispatcher acceptance is not presented as proof that the user saw the notification.
capabilities.next: run native Linux and Windows courts; retain typed unsupported results for subtitle/sound where the provider cannot promise those semantics
